**Question:** What should happen when the tool is given an invalid command line — an unrecognised flag such as `--redact-all`, for example? (FR-024, FR-025)

**Why it matters:** The spec currently defines only two exit statuses, 0 for success and 2 for an unreadable file, so there is no stated answer for a user who simply mistypes a flag. Without a decision, a test can't assert what happens, and the tool might silently ignore the flag and produce output the user thinks was processed differently.

**Recommended:** Option A — refusing to run on an unrecognised flag is what Constitution principle II (Fail Loudly) requires, and reusing status 2 keeps the contract to the two statuses the spec already documents rather than inventing a third.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Write a usage diagnostic naming the offending argument to standard error, produce no redacted output at all, and exit with status 2 |
| B | Same, but exit with a distinct status (e.g. 1) so callers can tell bad usage apart from an unreadable file |
| C | Ignore unrecognised flags and carry on redacting, exit status 0 |
| D | Treat an unrecognised argument as a filename, so it fails as an unreadable file via FR-025 |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended",ated or provide your own short answer.
